title: Interactive latency sliceboard for model+route with IO-mode temporal breakdown
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an interactive 'sliceboard' in Console that lets platform operators and SREs drill into end-to-end latency for a given model + route over time, with an explicit split between streaming (chunked responses) and non-streaming (sync) paths. The view should support p50/p95/p99, configurable time windows, traffic segmentation by client tag, and quick links to traces and logs.

Why: Current latency dashboards show route-level aggregates but lack fast, multidimensional slicing across IO mode and temporal windows. Teams are repeatedly asking for: (1) drift detection when streaming latency deviates from sync; (2) forensic workflows to jump from a percentile spike to related traces/logs/PRs; (3) lightweight comparison between two time ranges to validate rollouts.

Scope: Frontend sliceboard UI, backend aggregated metrics queries, new telemetry tags for io_mode where missing, trace linkback hooks, and alertable drift metrics. Minimal viable product (MVP) must include: p50/p95/p99 lines, an IO-mode toggle that overlays streaming vs sync percentiles, a heatmap by hour-of-day, and a "compare last N" time-range diff mode.

Telemetry: Add/standardize dimension: "io_mode" values ["streaming","sync","batch"] on request latency histogram buckets. Update ingestion pipeline to propagate this tag into the metrics store and ensure the tracing sampler includes io_mode for trace-context lookups. Provide example PromQL-like queries to power panels.

Acceptance criteria:
- Console sliceboard shows p50/p95/p99 for selected model+route and for the same selection with IO-mode overlay.
- Heatmap view of percentile across 24-hour window supports hover-to-filter by timestamp.
- 'Compare' mode highlights percentiles delta between base and compare ranges and marks deltas >10% in red.
- Each percentile point links to the top 3 representative traces and a log query pre-filled with timestamp + trace_id filter.
- Telemetry tag io_mode is present on >=95% of requests in staging and propagated to metrics within 15 minutes.
- Dashboard panels have documented queries and are included in the runtime-telemetry playbook.

Non-goals: Full A/B rollout analytics, advanced cost attribution, or embedding-level breakdowns (separate ticket).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Instrumentation (Backend): audit existing ingesters to ensure io_mode is emitted; where missing, add small middleware to set io_mode based on presence of streaming session headers. Add mapping for legacy clients to fallback to "sync".
2) Metrics pipeline: update aggregation job to maintain latency histograms keyed by [model, route, io_mode, region]. Add a derived metric for "io_mode_latency_delta" (p95_streaming / p95_sync).
3) Tracing hooks: add trace link template to sliceboard that points to trace explorer with io_mode and trace_id filters. Ensure sampling priorities in Canary routes.
4) Console UI: new sliceboard panel, heatmap, compare mode, and a lightweight timeseries overlay for percentiles. Mock-ups attached.
5) Alerts & playbook: define an alert when io_mode_latency_delta > 1.25 for 10m with traffic > 2qps and add runbook steps.

Risks/Trade-offs:
- Adding a new tag increases metrics cardinality; to mitigate we only emit io_mode for top-level request spans and sample low-volume routes.
- Heatmap and compare mode require efficient pre-aggregates; building them ad-hoc will have perf cost. We'll implement a 1-week rolling pre-aggregate and fall back to raw aggregation for queries outside the window.

Rollout plan:
- Staging: enable io_mode tagging and run sliceboard against staging dataset for 48h.
- Canary: enable for 10% of requests in us-west with dashboard monitoring.
- Global: enable full pipeline and ship release.

Docs & runbook: runtime-telemetry playbook will be updated with queries, alert thresholds, and troubleshooting steps.
